gap: No result ChatGPT got says that Bambu Studio's own PLA profile sets PLA's 'Softening temperature' (temperature_vitrification) at 45 °C but its default Textured PEI bed temperature at 55 °C. Bambu Studio's warning tooltip fires when the bed is at or above the softening temperature and tells you to open the front door and/or take off the upper glass to avoid nozzle clogs. So on an enclosed printer, textured PEI at its normal PLA setting only works with the enclosure open, while a cool-type plate at 35 °C stays under the limit.
standout_why: Pages compared: the cited Prusa KB PLA article (help.prusa3d.com/article/pla_2062) and the cited Flexible steel sheets guidepost (help.prusa3d.com/article/flexible-steel-sheets-guidepost_2195), plus the top results nozzlenotes.com (build plates) and 3dadapt.com (smooth vs textured vs satin). Prusa recommends a 60 °C bed and Satin/Smooth PEI for PLA, and says to let the sheet cool to room temperature before removing a print. Prusa never mentions enclosures, softening temperature or heat creep. The nozzlenotes page lists Bambu textured PEI at 45–60 °C for PLA but says nothing about a closed chamber. The 3dadapt page says outright that it does not cover Bambu plates or enclosed-printer heat. ChatGPT's own answer gives 50–60 °C for textured PEI, which is above Bambu's 45 °C softening value.
decides: For an enclosed printer (Bambu P1S, X1, P2S, X2D, or a QIDI Q2/Plus5/Max4), this changes the pick. Textured PEI at Bambu's own 55 °C default is 10 °C over the 45 °C softening value, so Bambu Studio will tell you to open the door or lift the lid. A cold-grip plate run at the bottom of its range (Bambu's Cool Plate profile is 35 °C; the BIQU Frostbite range on our page starts at 30 °C) lets the enclosure stay shut. The tooltip warns at 'equal to or greater than', so a plate run at 45 °C would also trigger it, as would the top of the Frostbite range (50 °C, figure from our page; I did not reopen it today). On the open-frame A1 and A1 mini this doesn't matter, and ChatGPT's pick, textured PEI, still stands.

findings.label: PLA softening temperature in Bambu Studio's generic PLA profile (temperature_vitrification)
findings.note: Read from the file: "temperature_vitrification": ["45"]. This is the base profile that Bambu's PLA filament presets inherit from.

findings.label: Default PLA bed temperature on the textured plate in Bambu Studio
findings.note: "textured_plate_temp": ["55"], "textured_plate_temp_initial_layer": ["55"]; hot_plate_temp (smooth PEI / High Temp plate) is also 55. 55 − 45 = 10 °C above the softening value.

findings.label: Default PLA bed temperature on the Cool Plate in Bambu Studio
findings.note: "cool_plate_temp": ["35"]. 45 − 35 = 10 °C below the softening value. eng_plate_temp is 0, which by Bambu's tooltip means PLA is not supported on the Engineering plate. The generic PLA file has no supertack_plate_temp key.

findings.label: What Bambu Studio does when the bed reaches the softening temperature
findings.value: Option labelled "Softening temperature". Tooltip: "The material softens at this temperature, so when the bed temperature is equal to or greater than it," followed by advice to open the front door and/or remove the upper glass to avoid clogs. Default 100 °C unless the filament profile overrides it.
findings.note: Read at offset 100000 of the file. The first clause is quoted exactly; the rest of the tooltip came back paraphrased (open front door and/or remove upper glass to avoid clogs), so quote only the first clause on the page.

findings.label: Prusa's recommended PLA bed temperature and surface
findings.value: 60 °C; "Satin or Smooth PEI sheet will provide the best adhesion"
findings.note: This is in the cited rival page, so it is not new. It is here for contrast: Prusa's 60 °C is 15 °C over Bambu's 45 °C softening value, which matters only in an enclosed chamber. Prusa also says "PLA does not require a heated bed."

findings.label: Named-reviewer note on cold-plate adhesion and removal
findings.value: "The bed adhesion strength when cold is immense!"; "even more essential to flex that plate"; thin prints will be troublesome
findings.source_title: Putting The New CryoGrip Build Plate To The Test (Hackaday, Dave Rowntree, 2024-10-25)
findings.note: Hackaday is summarising a test by the YouTube channel Printing Perspective. No temperatures or forces were measured. Hackaday's closed-door benefits (noise, filtration) are labelled as a guess, so they are not used as a finding.

unsourced: The Bambu wiki pages on heat creep, filament compatibility (PLA top glass/door advice above 45 °C) and HMS 0500-0400-0003-0009 ('keep the front door of printer open') all returned HTTP 402, so their exact wording comes only from search snippets and is left out.
